pros: Extremely simple to understand and implement
Computationally efficient with set intersection operations
Strong intuitive foundation in social theory (triadic closure)
No parameters to tune or configure
Serves as excellent baseline for comparing complex algorithms
Works well on sparse graphs with clear community structure
Naturally interpretable results (number of mutual friends)
Easy to parallelize for large-scale applications
cons: Treats all common neighbors equally, ignoring their importance
Favors high-degree nodes since they have more opportunities for overlap
Poor performance on dense graphs where many pairs share neighbors
Zero score for nodes without common neighbors limits coverage
Does not consider edge weights or connection strengths
Susceptible to bias towards popular/hub nodes
Limited discriminative power compared to normalized variants
